title: MV looking for a skill that absorbs damage on behalf of allies.

posts.author: Dehsalp
posts.body:
I have several characters in my party who play the tank role called 'Guard.' I am planning a skill where these allies absorb damage—either completely 'on behalf of' or a certain percentage—on behalf of other allies.
I am currently using multiple Yanfly plugins. Therefore, I have tried using the Taunt plugin (
https://www.yanfly.moe/wiki/Taunt_(YEP)
), but it is difficult to handle boss area-of-effect attacks or skills that target random enemies without specific targets using Taunt alone. Consequently, there are too many situations where the Guard becomes unnecessary, so I am looking for a skill that absorbs the damage on their behalf.
https://www.yanfly.moe/wiki/Damage_Dispersion_(MV_Plugin_Tips_&_Tricks)?utm_source=chatgpt.com
The closest I found was Damage Dispersion (
https://www.yanfly.moe/wiki/Damage_Dispersion_(MV_Plugin_Tips_&_Tricks)?utm_source=chatgpt.com
), but this is slightly different because it doesn't have the Guard absorb damage on behalf of the allies, but rather distributes the damage they receive to other allies.
I asked the GPT team just in case, and although they provided some code utilizing <Custom React Effect>, it didn't work at all.
Do happen to have any related information?

It depends on what it gave you. Chat GPT isnt going to give you functional code reliably, but a <Custom React Effect> can create an effect like the you're describing. It just requires Yanfly's Buffs and States Core plugin to implement the notetag in the first place, ideally the Passive Aura Effects plugin (for the all allies version) to make its application to all other party members and its duration tied to a "guard" state on the user, and the correct JS to go inside of the notetag.
Alternatively, you can use
taaspider's substitute plugin
to have better control over the substitute system and use it instead. Then you can set up your party guards, your single ally guards, remove the hp requirements, designate applicable damage types, etc.

Dehsalp said:
First, since I was just giving an example, it doesn't actually need to last infinitely. I am already using passive and buff & state plugins, and I believe I can make it last from the start by not specifying the duration of the state turns.
Click to expand...
Yanfly's auras don't last indefinitely. They last for however long the state they're attached to is active on the target. It means they can last indefinitely if the state doesn't have an end duration or is a passive, but if the base state has a duration, the auras have the same duration (and will also end on all allies automatically if the base state is removed early, or be extended on all allies if the duration of the base state is extended)
So with auras, you would have your tank target themself with a skill that gives them the "guardian" state. It'll last lets say 3 turns, and that state would have an aura effect to project the "guarded" state on all allies with that react effect. The code would need to change a little bit though.
Its entirely up to you. What I gave you already is how it should be if you're not using auras, but the state is applied to all other party members individually, the state isn't actually tied to the user, they all technically last for their own durations, and you have to add manual checks to remove the states or else it'll linger and you get situations like "the tank takes damage for an ally, dies, gets back up, and then dies again because the ally never lost the cover state"

That is the default effect of guard, yes. Specifically, it applies a state that reduces damage by about half (modified by the Guard Effect special parameter). But there's nothing to stop you from making a skill that applies that state to the whole party, instead of just the user. Then one actor would sacrifice their turn to reduce damage for the entire party.
It's clear now that that's not what you were looking for, however. It sounds like what you need is a plugin that modifies how Substitute works, or something that partly simulates the Substitute mechanic, and it even sounds like you've found what you needed, so I won't go into any more detail.

I couldn't remember if the Target Core required the selection core, which would mean you already are using it, or if the Selection Core required the Target core and you needed to add it. You bringing up those targeting notetags reminded me that the Selection Core needed the Target Core.
Now, you *can* use the Target core to prevent the skill from being executed on a target with a guard on them, but IMO the selection core's approach is better. Because of the difference between being able to target something and being able to select them, the Selection Core will prevent the player from wasting their turn if the target of a guard skill already has one. using the Target Core will make the skill go off and then not target its target. It's a little hard to describe to someone without them already knowing what it is or seeing it.
Dehsalp said:
However, how do I prevent allies who are in a 'specific category state' from being selected?
It seems like I could do this by utilizing the code from the state category plugin in the <Custom Target Text> or <Custom Target Eval>
Click to expand...
I'll describe it with both the target core and the selection core so you can try out both and see what I mean.
With the selection core, you don't actually need any code for this. You can if you want, but it provides a notetag that lets you say the requirements to be able to select someone without code
Code:
<Select Conditions>
Not User
Not State: Guard A
Not State: Guard B
Not State: Guard C
</Select Conditions>
and that makes it so that the player can't select the user or anyone with any of the guards on them.
With the Target core, it'd require code and would be like this:
Code:
<Custom Target Eval>
if (target != user && !target.isStateCategoryAffected('Protected'))
  targets.push(target);
</Custom Target Eval>
But, as the target core doesn't restrict selection, it doesn't prevent you from wasting your turn. Like, it won't prevent the tank from selecting themself for guard, but the skill will not target them and will instead do nothing and waste their turn.
For the guard skill thats meant to target all allies, the Selection Core notetag doesn't have to change. the Target Core's would need to change to be this to target all allies except the user and whoever has one of your guard states in them. this uses the state category so you don't have to list the states
Code:
<Custom Target Eval>
user.friendsUnit().aliveMembers().forEach(ally => {
  if (ally != user && !ally.isStateCategoryAffected('Protected'))
    targets.push(ally);
})
</Custom Target Eval>

Robro33 said:
ah. no worries, i see now.
As mentioned, what I was referring to wasn't the Target Core, but the Selection Core.
I couldn't remember if the Target Core required the selection core, which would mean you already are using it, or if the Selection Core required the Target core and you needed to add it. You bringing up those targeting notetags reminded me that the Selection Core needed the Target Core.
Now, you *can* use the Target core to prevent the skill from being executed on a target with a guard on them, but IMO the selection core's approach is better. Because of the difference between being able to target something and being able to select them, the Selection Core will prevent the player from wasting their turn if the target of a guard skill already has one. using the Target Core will make the skill go off and then not target its target. It's a little hard to describe to someone without them already knowing what it is or seeing it.
I'll describe it with both the target core and the selection core so you can try out both and see what I mean.
With the selection core, you don't actually need any code for this. You can if you want, but it provides a notetag that lets you say the requirements to be able to select someone without code
Code:
<Select Conditions>
Not User
Not State: Guard A
Not State: Guard B
Not State: Guard C
</Select Conditions>
and that makes it so that the player can't select the user or anyone with any of the guards on them.
With the Target core, it'd require code and would be like this:
Code:
<Custom Target Eval>
if (target != user && !target.isStateCategoryAffected('Protected'))
  targets.push(target);
</Custom Target Eval>
But, as the target core doesn't restrict selection, it doesn't prevent you from wasting your turn. Like, it won't prevent the tank from selecting themself for guard, but the skill will not target them and will instead do nothing and waste their turn.
For the guard skill thats meant to target all allies, the Selection Core notetag doesn't have to change. the Target Core's would need to change to be this to target all allies except the user and whoever has one of your guard states in them. this uses the state category so you don't have to list the states
Code:
<Custom Target Eval>
user.friendsUnit().aliveMembers().forEach(ally => {
  if (ally != user && !ally.isStateCategoryAffected('Protected'))
    targets.push(ally);
})
</Custom Target Eval>
Click to expand...
Ah, I was being silly. I was actually already using the Selection Core, lol.
I was using a note tag with information like <Enemy or Actor Select>, and I thought it was the Target Core, but it turns out it was the Selection Core. Since I took a break for a few years due to personal reasons, I must have forgotten.
In that case, as an example:
<Select Conditions>
Not User
Not State: Guard A
Not State: Guard B
Not State: Guard C
</Select Conditions>
You wrote this, but according to the Selection Core, the part where it says "Guard A" is supposed to be the actual 'skill name' used in-game.
In that case, do I have to add a line for every increase in the number of protection skills?
ex) For Skill A:
<Select Conditions>
Not User
Not State: Guard B
Not State: Guard C
</Select Conditions>
For Skill B:
<Select Conditions>
Not User
Not State: Guard A
Not State: Guard C
</Select Conditions>
For Skill C:
<Select Conditions>
Not User
Not State: Guard A
Not State: Guard B
</Select Conditions>
Is it correct to write it like this?
Additionally, if Skills D, E, and F are created, do I have to add Not State: Guard D ... E ... F... to every single skill? Is it not possible to make selection impossible at once by utilizing categories? Or, if not, is it possible, but is this method much more stable?
As another question, does this only make 'selection' impossible?
For example, there are three characters in a party named X, Y, and Z.
And Y used Skill A on X to apply State A and protect X. However, regardless of the target, the skill C targets all allies. In this case, if Z uses C to apply the status effect C to all allies and thus protects them, what happens?
1. Since A is already applied to X, X is not designated as a target, nor is it applied to skills that target all allies. Therefore, only A remains on X, and C is not applied.
2. The A applied to X disappears, and C takes priority and overwrites it.
3. Both A and C are stacked on X, causing the problem to persist.
EDIT) Sorry! i missed the last part of the text because it was cut off by the translator; I see that I just need to put that in the note tags for area protection.
I think you only need to answer the first question!

Dehsalp said:
You wrote this, but according to the Selection Core, the part where it says "Guard A" is supposed to be the actual 'skill name' used in-game.
In that case, do I have to add a line for every increase in the number of protection skills?
Click to expand...
Has to be the state name or it can be the state's ID, but yeah, the no code version needs to have a line for each one. I mentioned it because you only mentioned 3 states till now and I figured a line for each wouldn't have been a hassle. If you do want to add more, you can use this and it'll go off of the state category instead. You wont have to add any more lines, you'd just need to make sure new states have the category tag.
Code:
<Custom Select Condition>
condition = target != user && !target.isStateCategoryAffected('Protected');
</Custom Select Condition>

</Custom Select Condition>
Since it might be difficult to understand the Korean, I will also write down the translated version.
EDIT ++) Ah, wait. i was stupid..
I was putting what should have been in the 'skill' note tag into the 'state' note tag (Idiot lol).
It works now that I've put it in the skill!
What I've tried so far is that if I use Protection on the same target in the same turn, target selection becomes impossible, so it switches to a different target.
I will test it a bit more.
EDIT +++)
Yes, it seems to work well in various situations.
Thank you!
I think I can use this code as is until any other issues arise in the future!
Thank you very much.
EDIT ++++)
If there is exactly one problem I found, it is when blocking area-of-effect attacks.
Let's assume an enemy attacks 8 allies, with 1 serving as a Guard and the remaining 7 all having protection buffs applied. The enemy uses an area-of-effect skill to attack all allies. However, no matter how much damage is inflicted exceeding the Guard's HP, only the Guard is knocked down; the excess damage is not calculated. It is as if the damage calculation treated the Guard as having taken a barrage of hits.
Ah, of course, I am not asking for the exact excess damage to be calculated.
For example, if HP is 500 and DAMAGE is 1000 + 1000, I am not asking to subtract 500 to calculate 500 and 1000 separately!
I believe it is correct to take damage equivalent to the HP excess once.
EX2) Taking the example above as is, with HP 500 and DAMAGE 1000 + 1000, blocking 1000 damage once causes the guard to fall, and then blocking the 1000 damage from a second different actor. I was considering the feasibility of this.
Of course, this is not strictly necessary. I believe both approaches have their pros and cons. However, since this tended to make the difficulty significantly easier, it made me think about the matter.
